name: is_retryable_error
prose: Precondition: none; error is any int (callers pass negative errno values) (smb/client/cifsglob.h:1847-1852, static inline bool is_retryable_error(int error)). Postcondition: returns true when is_interrupt_error(error) is true or error == -EAGAIN, and false otherwise. is_interrupt_error (cifsglob.h:1835-1845) is true for -EINTR, -ERESTARTSYS, -ERESTARTNOHAND and -ERESTARTNOINTR only (not -ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK). So the function returns true exactly for -EINTR, -ERESTARTSYS, -ERESTARTNOHAND, -ERESTARTNOINTR and -EAGAIN. It reads and writes no state.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (\result != 0) <==> (error == -4 || error == -11 || error == -512 || error == -513 || error == -514); */
note: slice cut head (function at 1847-1852, slice 1847-2099). reviewer round 15 right that -516 (ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK) is not in is_interrupt_error's list; verified at cifsglob.h:1837-1844. The contract uses the Linux values EINTR 4, EAGAIN 11, ERESTARTSYS 512, ERESTARTNOINTR 513, ERESTARTNOHAND 514 (negated), as constants; drop it if the verifier rejects raw errno numbers.

name: CIFSGetExtAttr
prose: Precondition: xid is the transaction id, tcon is NULL or a valid cifs_tcon with a usable session, netfid is the file handle to query, pExtAttrBits and pMask are writable pointers (smb/client/cifssmb.c:3595-3673, compiled under CONFIG_POSIX, int CIFSGetExtAttr(const unsigned int xid, struct cifs_tcon *tcon, const int netfid, __u64 *pExtAttrBits, __u64 *pMask); the packet name CIFSSMBGetExtAttr does not exist). Postcondition: returns 0 with *pExtAttrBits and *pMask set from the 16-byte file_chattr_info in the response; -ENODEV at line 3606 if tcon is NULL; the error of smb_init at 3612 if the request buffer cannot be set up (returned directly without a retry, so this error can be -EAGAIN); otherwise it builds a TRANS2_QUERY_FILE_INFORMATION request with information level SMB_QUERY_ATTR_FLAGS and sends it with SendReceive. If SendReceive fails its error is returned, except -EAGAIN which makes the function release the request buffer and resend the whole request (label GetExtAttrRetry, repeating without a bound). If SendReceive succeeds, validate_t2 failing or a byte count below 2 gives -EIO, and a data count other than 16 gives -EIO; the data is located by the data offset in the response and read without a further bounds check against the buffer. On every error path the two output pointers are left unmodified. The request buffer is released (cifs_buf_release) before returning on all paths after smb_init succeeded.
note: packet name CIFSSMBGetExtAttr does not exist (the real name is CIFSGetExtAttr, cifssmb.c:3595); the slice 3604-3856 starts inside it (slice cut head). The earlier prose said the SendReceive failure is 'never -EAGAIN'; that holds for SendReceive but smb_init's error is returned directly (3611-3612) and may be -EAGAIN, so the claim was too strong.

name: CIFSFindFirst
prose: Precondition: xid is the transaction id, tcon and tcon->ses are valid, searchName is the directory path (or empty), cifs_sb provides the codepage and mount flags, pnetfid is NULL or points to a __u16, search_flags is the SMB search flags, psrch_inf points to a cifs_search_info whose info_level is set, msearch selects a wildcard search over the directory (smb/client/cifssmb.c:4306-4457, int CIFSFindFirst(const unsigned int xid, struct cifs_tcon *tcon, const char *searchName, struct cifs_sb_info *cifs_sb, __u16 *pnetfid, __u16 search_flags, struct cifs_search_info *psrch_inf, bool msearch); the packet name CIFSSMBFindFirst does not exist). Postcondition: returns 0 on success, otherwise the error of smb_init (line 4328, returned directly with no retry, so it may be -EAGAIN), the SendReceive error (at 4425, after releasing the request buffer; -EAGAIN causes the whole request to be rebuilt and resent without a bound), or the validate_t2 error (4431, after releasing the buffer). On success the buffer is NOT released: psrch_inf is filled with unicode, ntwrk_buf_start = the response buffer (the caller becomes responsible for freeing it), smallBuf = false, srch_entries_start (at the response's data offset), endOfSearch, entries_in_buffer = SearchCount, index_of_last_entry = 2 + entries_in_buffer, and last_entry = srch_entries_start + LastNameOffset together with *pnetfid = the search handle when pnetfid is non-NULL; if LastNameOffset is larger than CIFSMaxBufSize it logs 'ignoring corrupt resume name', sets last_entry = NULL and leaves *pnetfid unset, still returning 0. The request builds the file name as UTF-16 (when the session uses Unicode, with an appended separator and '*' for msearch, or a lone separator for an empty name) or as a copied ASCII path (with the same additions), sets search attributes read-only|hidden|system|directory, a search count of one or CIFSMaxBufSize / sizeof(FILE_UNIX_INFO) entries for msearch, and the information level from psrch_inf->info_level.
note: packet name CIFSSMBFindFirst does not exist (real name CIFSFindFirst, cifssmb.c:4306); the slice 4375-4628 starts in its middle (slice cut head). Mechanical reviewers only; the previous prose is replaced since it was not checked against buffer ownership on success.

name: cifs_setup_ipc
prose: Precondition: ses is a valid session with a usable ses->server, seal says whether encryption is requested (smb/client/connect.c:2037-2081, struct cifs_tcon *cifs_setup_ipc(struct cifs_ses *ses, bool seal); the packet item was unnamed, and the slice 2044-2300 starts inside it, slice cut head). Postcondition: returns a new IPC tree connection or an ERR_PTR; single success return 'return tcon' at line 2080. If seal is true and the server lacks SMB2_GLOBAL_CAP_ENCRYPTION it logs and returns ERR_PTR(-EOPNOTSUPP) (2050) with nothing allocated. tcon_info_alloc failure returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) (2056). Otherwise it builds the UNC path \\<hostname>\IPC$ (reading server->hostname under srv_lock), sets tcon->ses = ses, tcon->ipc = true and tcon->seal = seal, and calls server->ops->tree_connect(xid, ses, unc, tcon, ses->local_nls) between get_xid and free_xid. If that fails it logs, frees the tcon with tconInfoFree and returns ERR_PTR(rc) (2072). On success it sets tcon->status = TID_GOOD under tc_lock and returns the tcon. Despite the header comment, this function does not store the tcon in ses->tcon_ipc; the caller owns the returned tcon and is expected to store it. No locks are held on return.
note: item unnamed; the function is cifs_setup_ipc (connect.c:2037-2081; slice 2044-2300 begins inside it and then continues into cifs_find_smb_ses, __cifs_put_smb_ses and cifs_set_cifscreds, which are not this item). Added the caveat that the header comment says the tcon is stored in the session but the code does not store it (no assignment to ses->tcon_ipc in 2037-2081).

name: cifs_negotiate_protocol
prose: Precondition: ses and server are valid, server->ops is set, the caller holds neither server->srv_lock nor other connection locks (smb/client/connect.c:4051-4104, int cifs_negotiate_protocol(const unsigned int xid, struct cifs_ses *ses, struct TCP_Server_Info *server)). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno through these return statements: -ENOSYS at 4058 if the ops lack need_neg or negotiate (state unchanged); -EHOSTDOWN at 4067 if server->tcpStatus is not CifsGood, CifsNew or CifsNeedNegotiate (state unchanged); 0 at 4073 if server->ops->need_neg(server) is false and tcpStatus is already CifsGood (no negotiation, state unchanged); and 'return rc' at 4103. Otherwise it sets tcpStatus = CifsInNegotiate and neg_start = jiffies under srv_lock and calls server->ops->negotiate(xid, ses, server). A result of -EAGAIN is retried once from the top (the status checks are repeated, so a changed tcpStatus can make the retry return -EHOSTDOWN or 0 early); a second -EAGAIN becomes -EHOSTDOWN. Afterwards, under srv_lock: on success (rc == 0) tcpStatus becomes CifsGood only if it is still CifsInNegotiate, else rc = -EHOSTDOWN; on any failure (including the converted -EHOSTDOWN) tcpStatus is set back to CifsNeedNegotiate only if it is still CifsInNegotiate. So the status is restored to CifsNeedNegotiate on failures after negotiation started, but not on the early -ENOSYS and -EHOSTDOWN returns.
note: slice cut head (function at 4051-4104, slice 3870-4120). reviewers: original right (the early -ENOSYS 4058 and -EHOSTDOWN 4067 returns leave tcpStatus unchanged); round 2 right (when need_neg is false and the status is CifsGood it returns 0 at 4073); round 15 right (after the second -EAGAIN, rc = -EHOSTDOWN at 4087 and the failure branch resets CifsInNegotiate to CifsNeedNegotiate at 4098-4099).

name: smb3_parse_opt
prose: Precondition: options and key are non-NULL NUL-terminated strings and val points to a char pointer (smb/client/fs_context.c:540-569, int smb3_parse_opt(const char *options, const char *key, char **val)). Postcondition: it duplicates options with kstrdup (-ENOMEM at line 547 if that fails, *val untouched), splits the copy on ',' and, skipping empty tokens, takes the first token whose first strlen(key) characters equal key (case-insensitive, strncasecmp) AND that contains an '=' not in the first position (so key need not be followed directly by '=': a token 'username=x' matches the key 'user', and the text after the first '=' is returned). For that token it sets *val = kstrdup(text after '=') and returns 0, or -ENOMEM with *val set to NULL if that copy fails. A token that begins with key but has no '=' is skipped and the scan continues, as is one whose '=' is the first character. If no token matches it returns -ENOENT and *val is not written. The duplicated options string is freed on every path. *val is written only in the match case (and set to NULL only on the allocation failure), not on all paths.
note: the slice (fs_context.c:1349-1649) is a middle part of smb3_fs_context_parse_param, but the item's name and prose describe smb3_parse_opt (fs_context.c:540-569), so it is fixed under that real name (slice does not contain it). reviewer round 15 wrong on all three points: the comparison is strncasecmp (case-insensitive, line 554), the key need not be followed by '=' (554-559), and *val is written only at 561 (set to NULL only if kstrdup fails).

name: smb3_fs_context_parse_param
prose: Precondition: fc is a cifs/smb3 fs_context whose private data is an smb3_fs_context, param is one parsed mount parameter (smb/client/fs_context.c:1125-1848, static int smb3_fs_context_parse_param(struct fs_context *fc, struct fs_parameter *param); the packet name cifs_parse_mount does not exist and slice 1650-1903 is the tail of this function). Postcondition: returns 0 if the option was accepted and applied to the context, or -EINVAL at 1847 via cifs_parse_mount_err, which frees and NULLs ctx->password, ctx->password2, ctx->source and fc->source before returning; there is also an early return at 1157: the negative fs_parse result, or 1 (not an error) when the sloppy option is set and the option is unknown. String options with an empty value (pass, password, user, username, pass2, password2) bypass fs_parse and are handled directly. The tail of the switch (1650 onward) handles: unix/posix extensions (conflicting settings only warn), nocase, brl (turning it off also changes file_mode when it has the default mandatory-lock form), handlecache, forcemandatorylock, setuids, intr, setuidfromacl, strictsync, serverino, rwpidforward, modesid, cifsacl, acl, locallease, sign, ignore_signature, seal, noac (only a warning), fsc (-EINVAL via the error label when the kernel lacks CONFIG_CIFS_FSCACHE), mfsymlinks, multiuser, sloppy, nosharesock, persistent and resilient handles (conflicting combinations such as persistent with nopersistent or resilient give -EINVAL), tcp_nodelay, domainauto, rdma, reparse and symlink flavors (a failing flavor parser gives -EINVAL) and symlinkroot (must be an absolute path shorter than PATH_MAX, else -EINVAL; the string pointer is taken over from param). After the switch, multiuser together with upcalltarget 'mount' gives -EINVAL, and multichannel is cleared when max_channels is 1; then it returns 0.
note: item named cifs_parse_mount (dropped as not-in-slice); that name does not exist: the slice 1650-1903 is the tail of smb3_fs_context_parse_param (fs_context.c:1125-1848; slice cut head), so FIXED under the real name per rule 6. The earlier prose was a general summary and did not list the exits (1157, 1836, 1847).

name: cifs_ses_add_channel
prose: Precondition: ses is a valid session with ses->chan_count >= 1 and room for one more channel in ses->chans; iface is the server interface (address, speed, rdma capability) to use for the new channel (smb/client/sess.c:486-645, int cifs_ses_add_channel(struct cifs_ses *ses, struct cifs_server_iface *iface); the packet name cifs_setup_channel does not exist). Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno; the single return is 'return rc' at 644 after free_xid. It builds a temporary smb3_fs_context (kzalloc; -ENOMEM at 521 if that fails, going to out_free_xid), copying authentication, signing, unicode and version fields from the session and its main server, a UNC of the form \\<ses->ip_addr>\foo (kzalloc failure gives -ENOMEM via out_free_ctx), the interface's destination address and rdma capability, and the main connection's client GUID, with nosharesock set so a new connection is always made. It calls cifs_get_tcp_session(ctx, ses->server); under ses->chan_lock the result is stored in ses->chans[ses->chan_count].server: an error pointer is converted (rc = PTR_ERR, the slot's server set to NULL, lock released) and goes to out without incrementing chan_count; otherwise the slot gets the interface, chan_count is incremented, chan_seq reset, the channel marked as needing reconnect. Under ses->session_mutex it allocates the channel's crypto (smb3_crypto_shash_allocate; error: unlock and out), runs cifs_negotiate_protocol and, if that succeeded, cifs_setup_session (their error becomes rc). On failure after the channel was added (rc != 0 and the slot's server non-NULL) it drops the new connection with cifs_put_tcp_session, clears the need-reconnect bit and decrements ses->chan_count under chan_lock (WARN_ON if it would drop below 1). It then frees ctx->UNC and ctx (the strings other than UNC borrowed from the session are not freed).
note: packet name cifs_setup_channel does not exist; real function cifs_ses_add_channel at sess.c:486-645; the slice 508-763 starts inside it (slice cut head). Mechanical reviewers only; the earlier prose is replaced because it described a function with another name.

name: cifs_check_trans2
prose: Precondition: mid is the mid_q_entry for the response just received on server, buf is the received SMB buffer, malformed is non-zero when the buffer was already found malformed (smb/client/smb1transport.c:727-763, returns bool; static, the caller is the SMB1 receive path). Postcondition: returns true when the response should continue to be handled as a (possibly multi-part) trans2 response, false when it should be handled as an ordinary response. Return points: (1) if malformed is non-zero or check2ndT2(buf) <= 0 (not a secondary trans2 fragment): if mid->multiRsp is already set it sets multiEnd = true, dequeues the mid (dequeue_mid(mid, true)) and returns true (738); otherwise returns false (740). (2) Otherwise this is a fragment: mid->multiRsp is set. If mid->resp_buf already holds the first part, coalesce_t2(buf, mid->resp_buf) is called: it copies this fragment's data into the end of the stored first buffer and returns 1 when more parts are expected (the fragment has then already been copied into the target, and check_trans2 returns true at 747 leaving the mid queued), or 0 when all parts have arrived, or a negative errno (-EPROTO, -ENOBUFS) when the data is inconsistent; for 0 or a negative value multiEnd is set, the mid is dequeued (dequeue_mid(mid, malformed), where malformed is that result) and it returns true (751). (3) If this is the first part (no resp_buf): when server->large_buf is false it only logs '1st trans2 resp needs bigbuf' and returns true without keeping buf (line 762); when it is true the buffer is attached to the mid (mid->resp_buf = buf, mid->large_buf = true) and server->bigbuf is set to NULL, so the mid owns the buffer, and it returns true.
note: slice cut head (function at 727-763, slice 505-763). reviewers all right: original (the first fragment with !server->large_buf neither claims buf nor clears server->bigbuf yet returns true, 753-755, 762); round 2 (the multiRsp branch at 735-738 and the completed/error coalesce at 749-751 dequeue the mid, it is not kept in the queue); round 15 (coalesce_t2 copies the fragment before returning 1: smb1transport.c:713-718).

name: SMB2_change_notify
prose: Precondition: tcon is a valid tree connection with tcon->ses non-NULL to be dereferenced, persistent_fid and volatile_fid identify an open directory handle, watch_tree and completion_filter select what to watch, max_out_data_len is passed to the caller's design (unused here), out_data points to a char pointer, plen is NULL or points to a u32 (smb/client/smb2pdu.c:4052-4149, int SMB2_change_notify(const unsigned int xid, struct cifs_tcon *tcon, u64 persistent_fid, u64 volatile_fid, bool watch_tree, u32 completion_filter, u32 max_out_data_len, char **out_data, u32 *plen); the packet name SMB2_notify does not exist). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno. It picks a channel with cifs_pick_channel(ses); if ses or the server is NULL it returns -EIO at 4077 without touching *plen or *out_data. Otherwise (label replay_again) it sets *plen = 0 when plen is non-NULL, builds the request with SMB2_notify_init (its error goes to cnotify_exit), and, on a replay, sleeps cur_sleep ms and marks the request as a replay; it sends and waits with cifs_send_recv. If that fails it counts the failure and keeps its error. On success, if the response buffer is NULL or shorter than sizeof(struct smb2_change_notify_rsp) + 1 it exits with rc = 0, *out_data untouched and *plen 0; else it validates the output buffer offset and length with smb2_validate_iov (error: exit with it), and kmemdups the OutputBufferLength bytes at OutputBufferOffset into *out_data: failure gives -ENOMEM and *out_data = NULL; success sets *plen to OutputBufferLength (when plen is non-NULL) and the caller owns the buffer and must kfree it. cnotify_exit releases the request small buffer and the response buffer; if the result is a replayable error (is_replayable_error) and smb2_should_replay allows another attempt, the whole sequence restarts at replay_again; otherwise it returns rc at 4148. The function returns 0 both for a real notification and for an empty or short response, so the caller must look at *out_data / *plen.
note: packet name SMB2_notify does not exist; real function is SMB2_change_notify (smb2pdu.c:4052-4149); slice 4068-4322 starts inside it (slice cut head). Mechanical reviewers only. max_out_data_len is not used in the function body (4052-4149), noted; the earlier prose described the signature differently.

name: smbd_negotiate
prose: Precondition: sc is an SMB Direct socket whose status should be SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_NEGOTIATE_NEEDED (a WARN_ON_ONCE fires otherwise but the function continues) (smb/client/smbdirect.c:1640-1680, static int smbd_negotiate(struct smbdirect_socket *sc)). Postcondition: returns 0 when the socket reached SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_CONNECTED, else a negative errno. It takes a receive buffer with get_receive_buffer, sets sc->status = SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_NEGOTIATE_RUNNING and sc->recv_io.expected = SMBDIRECT_EXPECT_NEGOTIATE_REP, and posts the receive (smbd_post_recv): on failure it returns that error after put_receive_buffer, with the status left at NEGOTIATE_RUNNING. It then posts the negotiate request (smbd_post_send_negotiate_req); its error is returned at 1661 directly (the receive buffer is not returned here and the status stays NEGOTIATE_RUNNING). Then it waits interruptibly (wait_event_interruptible_timeout on sc->status_wait for the status to leave NEGOTIATE_RUNNING, up to negotiate_timeout_msec). If the status is CONNECTED afterwards it returns 0. Otherwise: a wait result of 0 (timeout) gives -ETIMEDOUT, -ERESTARTSYS gives -EINTR, and anything else (the status changed to something other than CONNECTED) gives -ENOTCONN; on a timeout or signal this function does not change the status, which can still be NEGOTIATE_RUNNING when it returns.
note: slice cut head (function at 1640-1680, slice 1526-1778). reviewers right: original (the early post-send error returns the post's errno with the status still RUNNING, 1659-1661); round 2 (on timeout or signal the status is not changed by this function, 1672-1679).

name: ndr_decode_v4_ntacl
prose: Precondition: n is an initialised NDR reader over a buffer (n->length bytes) holding an encoded v4 NT ACL xattr, acl is a writable struct xattr_ntacl (smb/server/ndr.c:450-513, int ndr_decode_v4_ntacl(struct ndr *n, struct xattr_ntacl *acl); the packet item was unnamed and the slice 507-514 is the tail of this function, slice cut head). Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno; the single return statements are early returns of ndr_read_* errors or -EINVAL, and 'return ret' at 513. It resets n->offset = 0, then reads in order: a 16-bit version into acl->version (must be 4, else -EINVAL); a 32-bit second version that must equal acl->version (else -EINVAL); a 16-bit level and a 32-bit reference id (both discarded); a 16-bit hash type into acl->hash_type; XATTR_SD_HASH_SIZE bytes into acl->hash; then 10 bytes into acl->desc, whose result is not checked, so if fewer than 10 bytes remain acl->desc is not written; acl->desc must begin with the 9 characters 'posix_acl' (strncmp, else -EINVAL with a log); a 64-bit time (discarded); XATTR_SD_HASH_SIZE bytes into acl->posix_acl_hash; then it sets acl->sd_size = n->length - n->offset (all remaining bytes), allocates acl->sd_buf with kzalloc (-ENOMEM if that fails) and copies the remaining bytes into it, returning the read result. Each ndr_read_* helper (for example ndr_read_bytes, ndr_read_int*) returns -EINVAL if the field would extend past n->length, so a truncated buffer yields -EINVAL; on any error after the allocation acl->sd_buf stays allocated and the caller owns and must free it, and on earlier errors previously decoded fields of acl remain set.
note: item unnamed; the slice 507-514 is the last lines of ndr_decode_v4_ntacl (ndr.c:450-513); FIXED under the real name (slice cut head). Mechanical reviewers only.

name: smb2_get_reparse_tag_special_file
prose: Precondition: mode is a Unix file mode (smb/server/smb2pdu.c:742-759, static __le32 smb2_get_reparse_tag_special_file(umode_t mode)). Postcondition: returns the little-endian SMB reparse tag for the file type in mode, or 0. It returns 0 (line 745) for a directory or a regular file; IO_REPARSE_TAG_LX_SYMLINK_LE (748) for a symbolic link; IO_REPARSE_TAG_LX_FIFO_LE (750) for a FIFO; IO_REPARSE_TAG_AF_UNIX_LE (752) for a socket; IO_REPARSE_TAG_LX_CHR_LE (754) for a character device; IO_REPARSE_TAG_LX_BLK_LE (756) for a block device; and 0 (758) for any other mode. The tags are the byte-swapped (cpu_to_le32) constants of the same names, whose numeric values are defined in the headers and are not restated here. The function reads and writes no state.
note: slice cut head (function at 742-759, slice 512-771). Round 2 reviewer pointed out that the earlier contract's numeric tag values were wrong; the prose now names the constants instead, and the contract is left empty for that reason (the _LE macros are byte-swapped constants the verifier cannot see).

name: smb2_ioctl
prose: Precondition: work is a ksmbd_work holding a received SMB2 IOCTL request (in work->request_buf, or the next command of a compound request) and a response buffer; the connection and tree connection are set (smb/server/smb2pdu.c:8413-8780, int smb2_ioctl(struct ksmbd_work *work); the item was marked dropped as 'enclosing dispatcher' but smb2_ioctl is a real function and the slice 8474-8737 is its middle, slice cut head and tail). Postcondition: returns 0 when the response was built and pinned (line 8763) or a negative errno after setting rsp->hdr.Status and calling smb2_set_err_rsp (8778-8779); the early return of a non-zero pin result also goes to out. Setup: it selects req and rsp (the compound case uses the next-command buffers and the compound file id when the request's VolatileFileId is not a real id), takes id = req->VolatileFileId when no compound id applies, and requires req->Flags == SMB2_0_IOCTL_IS_FSCTL (-EOPNOTSUPP otherwise); smb2_calc_max_out_buf_len negative sets STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER and fails. Dispatch on CtlCode: FSCTL_DFS_GET_REFERRALS(_EX): -EOPNOTSUPP with STATUS_FS_DRIVER_REQUIRED (goes to out2, skipping the generic status mapping); FSCTL_CREATE_OR_GET_OBJECT_ID: a zero-filled object-id reply (dummy); FSCTL_PIPE_TRANSCEIVE: nbytes from fsctl_pipe_transceive; FSCTL_VALIDATE_NEGOTIATE_INFO: -EOPNOTSUPP for dialects before SMB3.0, -EINVAL for a short input or output buffer, else fsctl_validate_negotiate_info (a negative result fails) and the file ids set to SMB2_NO_FID; FSCTL_QUERY_NETWORK_INTERFACE_INFO: nbytes from fsctl_query_iface_info_ioctl; FSCTL_REQUEST_RESUME_KEY: -EINVAL for a short output buffer, else fsctl_request_resume_key; FSCTL_COPYCHUNK and FSCTL_COPYCHUNK_WRITE: -EACCES if the tree is not writable, -EINVAL for short in/out buffers, then fsctl_copychunk fills the response; FSCTL_SET_SPARSE: -EINVAL for a short input, else fsctl_set_sparse; FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA: -EACCES if not writable, -EINVAL for short input or an invalid [offset, beyond-final-zero) range, and for a non-empty range -ENOENT if the file id is unknown, -EACCES without FILE_WRITE_DATA, else ksmbd_vfs_zero_data; FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES: -EINVAL for a short input, -E2BIG sets STATUS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW but still returns the ranges found, other negatives fail; FSCTL_GET_REPARSE_POINT: -ENOENT if the file id is unknown, else the reparse tag from smb2_get_reparse_tag_special_file of the file mode with zero data length; FSCTL_DUPLICATE_EXTENTS_TO_FILE: -EINVAL for short input, -ENOENT for an unknown source or target handle, -EACCES if the tree is read-only or the target lacks write or the source lacks read access, then vfs_clone_file_range (-EXDEV and -EOPNOTSUPP give -EOPNOTSUPP) and, for any other short clone, vfs_copy_file_range, with an error or short copy giving the negative error or -EINVAL; every other control code gives -EOPNOTSUPP. On success it fills the response header (CtlCode, InputCount 0, offsets 112, OutputCount = nbytes, StructureSize 49) and pins it with ksmbd_iov_pin_rsp. The error exit maps -EACCES to STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED, -ENOENT to STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND, -EOPNOTSUPP to STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED, -ENOSPC to STATUS_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, and any other negative value or a status still 0 to STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER.
note: item smb2_ioctl dropped as 'enclosing dispatcher' with a one-line prose; smb2_ioctl is a real function (smb2pdu.c:8413-8780) and per rule 6 it is FIXED. The slice 8474-8737 contains only part of the switch (slice cut head and tail); the description covers the whole function. Handler helpers (fsctl_*) were not read.

name: smb21_lease_break_ack
prose: Precondition: work holds an SMB2 lease break acknowledgment request on an established connection (work->conn) (smb/server/smb2pdu.c:8920-8992, static void smb21_lease_break_ack(struct ksmbd_work *work); returns nothing and reports errors in the response header). Postcondition: it looks up the lease by req->LeaseKey in the connection's lease table (lookup_lease_in_table). If none is found it calls smb2_set_err_rsp(work), then sets rsp->hdr.Status = STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL and returns (no oplock_info to release). If found (a reference is held on opinfo), it takes the error exit err_out (smb2_set_err_rsp(work) and opinfo_put) with these statuses set before the call: STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL if opinfo->op_state is OPLOCK_STATE_NONE or breaking_cnt is zero; STATUS_REQUEST_NOT_ACCEPTED if check_lease_state(lease, req->LeaseState) rejects the requested state. Otherwise it sets lease->state = req->LeaseState, lease->new_state = SMB2_LEASE_NONE_LE and opinfo->level from the lease state, fills the acknowledgment response (StructureSize 36, same lease key, new lease state, duration 0) and pins it with ksmbd_iov_pin_rsp. If the pin fails it goes to err_out without setting a status of its own (only smb2_set_err_rsp is called), and the lease state changes already made are not undone. On success it sets op_state to OPLOCK_STATE_NONE under state_lock unless it is OPLOCK_CLOSING, wakes the oplock and break waiters, decrements breaking_cnt if positive (atomic_dec_if_positive) and drops the opinfo reference.
note: slice cut head (function at 8920-8992, slice 8738-8993). reviewers: original right (a missing lease key is handled, 8934-8940, with no opinfo to put); round 2 and round 15 right (on pin failure the code only calls smb2_set_err_rsp at 8989 and sets no status, 8974-8976, so the earlier claim that STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL is set there was wrong). I did not read smb2_set_err_rsp to say how it treats the header status.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(tee, int, fdin, int, fdout, size_t, len, unsigned int, flags)
prose: Generated system call tee(fdin, fdout, len, flags) (splice.c:1979-1996). Return values: -EINVAL at 1982 if flags has any bit outside SPLICE_F_ALL; 0 at 1985 if len == 0, without looking at either descriptor; -EBADF at 1989 if fdin is not open and at 1993 if fdout is not open; otherwise the result of do_tee(in, out, len, flags). do_tee (splice.c:1940-1977) returns -EBADF if the input file is not readable or the output file is not writable; -EINVAL if either file is not a pipe or both refer to the same pipe; otherwise it adds SPLICE_F_NONBLOCK when either file has O_NONBLOCK, calls ipipe_prep (input pipe) and opipe_prep (output pipe), and if both succeed link_pipe(ipipe, opipe, len, flags), returning the number of bytes duplicated (> 0), 0, or the negative error of whichever helper failed (a non-blocking call can return -EAGAIN, from either helper, depending on whether it has to wait; I did not read these helpers); on a positive result it issues fsnotify access and modify events. The data is duplicated by reference, not copied, and the input pipe's contents are not consumed. The descriptor references taken by the CLASS(fd) guards are released automatically.
note: macro-generated; name set to the SYSCALL_DEFINE4 head at splice.c:1979 (packet name __do_sys_tee). Reviewers: round 1 right that len == 0 returns 0 before touching the descriptors (1984-1985); round 2 plausible (-EAGAIN is not only for a full pipe) but depends on ipipe_prep/opipe_prep, which I did not read, so stated without detail. The SIGPIPE side effect mentioned by round 1 is in the pipe helpers, not verified here.

name: do_splice_read
prose: Precondition: in is an open file, ppos is its read position pointer (may be NULL for non-seekable files), pipe is the destination pipe with its lock held by the caller, len is the requested byte count, flags the SPLICE_F_* flags (splice.c:956-983, static ssize_t do_splice_read(struct file *in, loff_t *ppos, struct pipe_inode_info *pipe, size_t len, unsigned int flags)). Postcondition: returns -EBADF at 963 if in is not opened for reading (checked before len, so this applies even for len == 0); 0 at 965 if len is 0; otherwise len is clamped to the free pipe space (max_usage minus pipe_buf_usage, in pages) and to MAX_RW_COUNT, and the function returns -EINVAL (via warn_unsupported, which also logs a rate-limited debug message) at 975 if in->f_op->splice_read is NULL; copy_splice_read(in, ppos, pipe, len, flags) at 981 if the file is O_DIRECT or on a DAX inode; else in->f_op->splice_read(in, ppos, pipe, len, flags) at 982. In the last two cases the value returned is the underlying routine's result: the number of bytes spliced, 0 (for example at end of file or when the clamped length is 0 because the pipe is full), or a negative errno. So 0 is not returned only when len is 0.
note: slice cut head (function at 956-983, slice 778-1034). reviewers all right: round 1 (-EBADF is returned even for len == 0 because the f_mode check precedes the len check, 962-965; a missing splice_read gives -EINVAL not 0); round 15 (the result of splice_read/copy_splice_read can be 0, e.g. at EOF).

name: squashfs_xattr_handler
prose: Precondition: type is the on-disk xattr type value (prefix id in SQUASHFS_XATTR_PREFIX_MASK, optionally with the SQUASHFS_XATTR_VALUE_OOL bit) (squashfs/xattr.c:246-263, static const struct xattr_handler *squashfs_xattr_handler(int type); the packet name squashfs_xattr_handler_lookup does not exist). Postcondition: returns a pointer to one of three static handlers or NULL. It returns NULL at line 250 if type has any bit set outside SQUASHFS_XATTR_PREFIX_MASK | SQUASHFS_XATTR_VALUE_OOL. Otherwise it switches on type & SQUASHFS_XATTR_PREFIX_MASK (the out-of-line value bit is ignored): SQUASHFS_XATTR_USER returns &squashfs_xattr_user_handler, SQUASHFS_XATTR_TRUSTED returns &squashfs_xattr_trusted_handler and SQUASHFS_XATTR_SECURITY returns &squashfs_xattr_security_handler; any other prefix value returns NULL (261). It reads and writes no state.
note: packet name squashfs_xattr_handler_lookup does not exist; real function squashfs_xattr_handler at xattr.c:246-263 (slice 252-271 contains its switch and the handler array; slice cut head). reviewer round 15 wrong: the code does return NULL when bits outside the mask are set (xattr.c:248-250); only the VALUE_OOL bit is allowed and ignored.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(stat, const char __user *, filename,
prose: Generated system call stat(filename, statbuf) (stat.c:424-435, under __ARCH_WANT_OLD_STAT) writes a struct __old_kernel_stat. prose: Generated system call statx(dfd, filename, flags, mask, buffer) (stat.c:812-827). A bad filename pointer gives -EFAULT (or -ENOENT for an empty string without AT_EMPTY_PATH) from getname.

note: macro-generated; name set to the exact SYSCALL_DEFINE/COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE head in stat.c at the line cited. Reviewer round 15 right: when copy_to_user fails (-EFAULT) the user buffer may already be partly written, so 'statbuf unmodified' is not guaranteed.

prose: Generated compat system call newfstat(fd, statbuf) (stat.c:904-913): error = vfs_fstat(fd, &stat) (stat.c:276-282: -EBADF if fd is not open, else vfs_getattr of the file's path with STATX_BASIC_STATS, which can return the security hook or filesystem getattr error); if that is 0 it returns cp_compat_stat(&stat, statbuf), else the error. cp_compat_stat (stat.c:830-863) returns -EOVERFLOW if the device numbers do not fit the field widths, the inode number or link count do not fit, or the file size exceeds MAX_NON_LFS; -EFAULT if copy_to_user fails (the buffer may be partly written); else 0.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE2(statfs, const char __user *, pathname, struct compat_statfs __user *, buf)
prose: Generated compat system call statfs(pathname, buf) (statfs.c:303-310, under CONFIG_COMPAT): error = user_statfs(pathname, &tmp); if that is 0 it returns put_compat_statfs(buf, &tmp), else the error. user_statfs (statfs.c:97-113) resolves the path (following symlinks, automounting) with user_path_at (its error is returned, -EFAULT/-ENOENT/-ENAMETOOLONG etc.), then vfs_statfs (statfs_by_dentry error such as -ENOSYS, or 0 with f_flags from the mount), retrying once with LOOKUP_REVAL on -ESTALE, and releasing the path. put_compat_statfs (statfs.c:265-297) returns -EOVERFLOW when the compat layout has 4-byte counters and f_blocks, f_bfree, f_bavail, f_bsize or f_frsize do not fit in 32 bits, or f_files or f_ffree (other than the all-ones value) do not fit; -EFAULT if copy_to_user fails; else 0.
note: macro-generated; name set to the exact COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE head in statfs.c at the line cited (packet names were shortened). Unreviewed originally; rewritten from the source. When copy_to_user fails the user buffer may be partly written.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE2(ustat, unsigned, dev, struct compat_ustat __user *, u)
prose: Generated compat system call ustat(dev, u) (statfs.c:389-403): decodes the device number with new_decode_dev and calls vfs_ustat (statfs.c:234-244), which returns -EINVAL if no mounted superblock with that device exists (user_get_super), else the result of statfs_by_dentry on the superblock root (the superblock reference is dropped with drop_super). A non-zero result is returned; otherwise it fills a zeroed compat_ustat with f_tfree = free blocks and f_tinode = free inodes (without the 32-bit clamp used by the native version, so large values are truncated to the field width) and returns -EFAULT if copy_to_user fails, else 0.
